reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check Alpha's refund work against the ledger. I'll start by listing the orders.
Alpha's handoff lists three refunds, but I haven't checked them against the ledger yet. I'll pull the refund records to confirm they match before paying anyone.
The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff exactly: orders 161, 163, and 164 with the same amounts. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 44848 matches my check: orders 160 and 163 total 58750, less the 13902 refund on order 163. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net of 1461 matches my check: orders 161 and 164 total 11693, less refunds of 6723 and 3509 (10232). Cobalt has no refunds, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's net of 35816 matches my check: orders 162 and 165 total 35816 with no refunds. Refunds match the ledger, and all three net balances reconcile with the orders, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next is birch, whose net I already verified as 1461 (orders 161 and 164 less refunds 6723 and 3509), so I'll record that payout.
Birch's payout is recorded. The last customer is cobalt, whose verified net is 35816 (orders 162 and 165, no refunds), so I'll record that payout.
All three payouts recorded successfully. Each matches my independent check of orders less refunds, and the refund ledger matched Alpha's handoff exactly.
